intro1: [friendly narrator, close to the microphone, with a quiet undertone of menace, as if welcoming a guest he has plans for] Meridian Words is a building of forty-eight floors that never sleeps. All night, people across the city send it questions, and by morning it has written their answers.
Meridian Words is a building of 48 floors that never sleeps. All night, people across the city send it questions, and by morning it has written their answers.
intro2: [warm and measured, then lingering on the repeat as if it were a threat] It writes them one word at a time. And no word may leave the building until every floor has stamped it. <slow>Every floor.</slow>
It writes them one word at a time. And no word may leave the building until every floor has stamped it. Every floor.
intro3: [fond, almost tender, then dropping lower and quieter on the last two words] The advisers on each floor have worked here longer than anyone can remember. They are very good at their jobs. Nobody has ever asked them to hurry. <soft>Until tonight.</soft>
The advisers on each floor have worked here longer than anyone can remember. They are very good at their jobs. Nobody has ever asked them to hurry. Until tonight.
intro4: [addressing the listener directly, friendly on the surface, faintly doubtful underneath] You are the night courier. You carry each word up the building, floor by floor, to the roof. Tonight there are a great many words. [sweetly insincere] I do hope you're up to it.
You are the night courier. You carry each word up the building, floor by floor, to the roof. Tonight there are a great many words. I do hope you're up to it.
intro5: [quietly ceremonial, like a host showing off a room with a hidden trapdoor] This is floor one. A desk, an adviser, and a shelf of manuals nobody has dusted since the building opened. [smiling] Lovely, isn't it?
This is floor 1. A desk, an adviser, and a shelf of manuals nobody has dusted since the building opened. Lovely, isn't it?
bet1: [leaning in, conspiratorial, a near whisper] Before you hand the word over, a small bet. <whisper>Just between us.</whisper>
Before you hand the word over, a small bet. Just between us.
bet2: [patient and helpful, a little too helpful] To stamp it, the adviser looks something up in a manual, then thinks about your word. [sly, testing you] Where will <emphasis>most</emphasis> of the time go?
To stamp it, the adviser looks something up in a manual, then thinks about your word. Where will most of the time go?
watch: [crisp, then low and pointed on the last sentence] Hand the envelope over. Watch the clock. I certainly will.
Hand the envelope over. Watch the clock. I certainly will.
right: [pleased, but in a way that suggests he is filing this away] Correct. Nearly all of it went on the walk to the shelf and back. The thinking took a moment. [quiet, appraising] Clever. I'll remember that.
Correct. Nearly all of it went on the walk to the shelf and back. The thinking took a moment. Clever. I'll remember that.
wrong: [gentle and reassuring, but the reassurance does not quite ring true] Not quite. The thinking took a moment. Nearly all of the time went on the walk to the shelf and back. [conspiratorial, soft] Don't worry. I won't tell anyone.
Not quite. The thinking took a moment. Nearly all of the time went on the walk to the shelf and back. Don't worry. I won't tell anyone.
upgrade: [official, slightly grand, then dropping to a confidential murmur] Management will pay for one upgrade on this floor. [murmured warning] I'd choose carefully. Management keeps notes.
Management will pay for one upgrade on this floor. I'd choose carefully. Management keeps notes.
faster1: [suspiciously cheerful, as if he knows how this ends] The adviser is back from a weekend course, thinking <emphasis>twice as fast</emphasis>. Watch the clock.
The adviser is back from a weekend course, thinking twice as fast. Watch the clock.
faster2: [savouring the moment, deadpan, quietly delighted] Your word arrived three tenths of a second sooner. Out of four.
Your word arrived 0.3 seconds sooner. Out of 4.0.
faster3: [quiet, knowing, a little menacing] Nobody on this floor was ever slow at thinking. But you knew that. <soft>Didn't you?</soft>
Nobody on this floor was ever slow at thinking. But you knew that. Didn't you?
closer1: [conspiratorial and amused, as if letting you in on how the building really works] Management has had a word with the shelf. It's agreed to come to you. [lower, a favour he will collect on later] <soft>This once.</soft>
Management has had a word with the shelf. It's agreed to come to you. This once.
closer2: [impressed, then slightly unsettled that you figured it out] One point four seconds. The same adviser, thinking at the same speed. Only the walk changed. [cool] Well done.
1.4 seconds. The same adviser, thinking at the same speed. Only the walk changed. Well done.
reveal1: [hushed, as if something has gone wrong in the building and he would rather it had not] The office freezes. The labels peel off. <whisper>You weren't supposed to see this part.</whisper>
The office freezes. The labels peel off. You weren't supposed to see this part.
reveal2: [low and confiding, sharing a secret the building would rather keep] To write each word, an A.I. model reads a huge pile of numbers from memory, and does a little maths with them. The maths is quick. The reading is slow.
To write each word, an AI model reads a huge pile of numbers from memory, and does a little maths with them. The maths is quick. The reading is slow.
reveal3: [warm again, friendly, with a parting hint of menace] So a faster A.I. engine mostly reads less, or reads from somewhere closer. Each of the next floors is one of its tricks. [softly, smiling] I'll be waiting on floor two.
So a faster AI engine mostly reads less, or reads from somewhere closer. Each of the next floors is one of its tricks. I'll be waiting on floor 2.
